newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to announce coffee export cuts next week.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to announce coffee export cuts next week.

text.p: Colombia will announce cuts in coffee exports next week under the terms of a beefed up retention plan agreed January 23 by members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries, National Coffee Growers' Federation chief Jorge Cardenas said.
He declined to say how much Colombia was likely to cut its exports but under the ACPC deal arabica-producing nations will hold back a total 300,000 60-kg bags in the first half of 1997.

"The arabica-producing countries took the decision (to hold back 300,000 bags of exports) in solidarity with robusta- producing nations. The cuts will respond to production conditions and the export situation in each individual country," Cardenas said.
"We will be announcing the cuts this will imply for Colombia next week," he added.
Cardenas also said the internal price of coffee would be raised in Colombia but declined to say excatly when the decision would be announced and what the percentage increase was likely to be.
"In view of the situation in external markets, we will of course have to raise the internal price of coffee. We will do the projections and take the decision on the basis of that," he said.
The federation effectively cut internal coffee prices by 14,000 pesos per 125-kg load to 221,500 after a turbulent coffee growers' congress on December 5.

The cut was achieved by withdrawing the 14,000 peso premium, paid in the form of a bond instead of cash, which had been introduced to compensate for the poor outlook for coffee in the 1996 calendar year.

As coffee growers voice mounting concern about unseasonal torrential rains that threaten to delay flowering and possibly destroy some of the main harvest, due to begin in October, Cardenas said federation technicians were drawing up a detailed report.
He said experts were waiting to get firmer details of the mid-term outlook and said a report on the specific impact of the abnormal weather conditions should be ready by mid-February.
